title: Standard Chess Legal-Play State and Semantics Contract

authority.primary: FIDE Laws of Chess taking effect from 1 January 2023, current in the FIDE Handbook when checked 2026-08-11
authority.scope_note: This contract formalizes the adversarial board-game/legal-play semantics needed for a weak solution. Tournament administration, clocks, conduct penalties, resignation and bilateral draw offers are not core graph actions. Claimable draws are core actions; automatic draws are core terminals.

board64.meaning: Piece placement only; piece identities beyond type/colour are not state.

castling_rights.meaning: Persistent historical rights. Rights are monotone: once lost they never return. A true right requires the corresponding king and rook to occupy their standard home squares.

ep_effective.meaning: En-passant target is retained only if at least one en-passant capture is legal in the current position. A merely nominal/pseudo-legal target that cannot be legally captured is canonicalized to null.

halfmove_clock.meaning: Number of halfmoves since the last pawn move or capture. A legal non-resetting move increments it by one. Pawn move or capture resets it to zero.

rep_counts.meaning: Occurrence counts since the most recent repetition barrier. Hashes may address keys on disk, but semantic identity is the raw canonical key; hash collision cannot define equality.

repetition_key.rationale: This captures the FIDE same-position test: same side to move, same piece placement, same move possibilities, with castling and en-passant rights handled explicitly.

full_state_identity.note: Full state identity is history-sensitive. Two identical boards can be different game states because claimability/automatic-draw futures differ.

repetition_barrier.effect: After the move, discard all earlier repetition counts and set rep_counts to {successor_repetition_key: 1}.
repetition_barrier.proof_obligation: Earlier repetition keys cannot recur after a barrier: pawn progress is monotone, captures reduce total piece count, and castling rights are monotone decreasing.

actions.board_move: Any legal move under standard chess movement, check, promotion, castling and en-passant rules.
actions.claim_threefold_now: Available if the current repetition key has occurred at least three times.
actions.claim_threefold_by_move: Available by naming a legal intended move whose resulting repetition key would be at least the third occurrence. The claim terminates the game as a draw before the move is executed.
actions.claim_fifty_by_move: Available by naming a legal intended non-pawn, non-capture move that would make halfmove_clock >= 100. The claim terminates the game as a draw before the move is executed.

automatic_terminals.checkmate: Immediate win for the player who delivered mate.
automatic_terminals.dead_position: Immediate draw iff no legal sequence from the position can ever reach checkmate by either player. Insufficient-material heuristics are not an exact substitute.
automatic_terminals.fivefold_repetition: Immediate draw when the current repetition key reaches occurrence count 5.
automatic_terminals.seventy_five_move: Immediate draw when halfmove_clock reaches 150, except that checkmate delivered by that move takes precedence.

reachability_typing.LOCAL_ADMISSIBLE: Satisfies the declared local/state invariants and legal-move semantics; may be historically unreachable from the standard initial position.
reachability_typing.START_REACHABLE: There exists a legal full-state path from the standard initial state under this contract.
reachability_typing.rule: Backward/arena truth may be certified over LOCAL_ADMISSIBLE states. It can enter a final initial-position proof only at a full-state entry reached from an already START_REACHABLE parent, or with an explicit reachability certificate.

core_graph_exclusions.draw_by_agreement: Bilateral and therefore not a unilateral forced non-loss resource against an adversarial opponent; excluded from the core graph without changing the existence of a forced White non-loss strategy.
core_graph_exclusions.resignation: Voluntary concession; excluded because a non-losing strategy never needs to resign.
core_graph_exclusions.clock_forfeit_and_tournament_sanctions: Depend on event-specific time controls/administration rather than the abstract legal-play game graph; outside the weak-solution theorem declared here.

active_state_invariants: exactly one white king and one black king
side-to-move position is not already checkmate or stalemate
current repetition occurrence is less than 5
ep_effective is null unless a legal en-passant capture exists
castling rights are consistent with king/rook home-square occupancy
rep_counts contains the current repetition key with positive count
every rep_counts value is at most 4

serialization.semantic_form: Length-prefixed UTF-8 fields in the full_state_identity order; castling rights sorted KQkq; rep_counts sorted lexicographically by raw repetition-key bytes.
serialization.transport_digest: SHA-256 of semantic_form may be used for content addressing, but equality must be confirmed against canonical bytes on any digest collision.

versioning.breaking_change: Any change to state identity, claimability, terminal precedence, reachability typing or move legality increments the major contract version and invalidates unqualified truth hashes.
versioning.nonbreaking_change: Serialization container or implementation optimization that preserves canonical semantic bytes and transition relation may increment a minor implementation version.

derived_lemmas.G10-L1_HISTORY_BARRIER: After a pawn move, capture, or permanent castling-right reduction, no repetition key from before that move can ever recur. Therefore all earlier repetition counts may be discarded exactly.
derived_lemmas.G10-L2_COUNT_SUFFICIENCY: Within one barrier epoch, threefold/fivefold semantics depend only on the occurrence count of each repetition key, not the order in which those keys occurred. A sorted count map is therefore a semantics-preserving quotient of the ordered trace.
derived_lemmas.G10-L3_ACTIVE_COUNT_BOUND: No active state can contain a repetition-key count above 4, because the fifth occurrence is an automatic draw terminal.
derived_lemmas.G10-L4_HISTORY_FINITE: The history component is finite: between pawn moves/captures the 75-move rule terminates by 150 halfmoves, and castling-right reductions only shorten repetition epochs. Thus an active repetition-count map needs at most the keys encountered within the bounded current epoch.
